Page: /reference/svelte/package-scene.md

The runtime that draws declarative scenes (what Python sends) in any Svelte app.

### Example

```svelte
<script>
  import { initializePlot } from "hmplot";
  import { SceneRenderer, SceneRuntime } from "hmplot/scene";
  const runtime = new SceneRuntime((message) => console.log(message));
  // state: a scene (python/PROTOCOL.md); load(id): its binary columns.
  initializePlot().then(() => runtime.apply(state, load));
</script>

<SceneRenderer {runtime} />
```

### Exports

- `SceneRenderer` (`component`): Draws a runtime's scene: <SceneRenderer {runtime} />; notebook adds the notebook's frame around it; a Plot without a width fills it unless fill={false}.
- `SceneRuntime` (`class`): new SceneRuntime(send): one scene's state. apply(state, load) validates and draws a scene (load(id) resolves a binary column to { descriptor, payload }); settle(timeoutMs) waits until it is drawn; command({ command, target, args }) runs Python's commands (exports, camera, viewport, time, selection); dispose() frees it. send(message) receives what Python would: status, events, input values, interaction and offsets.
- `SceneResources` (`class`): The tables, scales, selections and identities a runtime holds (runtime.resources); apply prepares them.
- `sceneRegistry` (`object`): The components a scene may name, their properties and settings, and the protocol version (the registry.json Python ships too).

### Usage

Python builds a scene as data, a tree of components with their props and binary columns, and the browser draws it with this runtime: the notebook widget, exported HTML pages and Python's headless exports all use it. Use it to draw a scene that Python (or your own code) produced, in any Svelte app: a dashboard that loads a scene saved by Python, or another transport than Jupyter's.

`runtime.apply(state, load)` checks and draws a scene: `state` is a scene message's state (its protocol version, revision and root node, and the columns, tables and other resources its nodes name), and `load(id)` returns, or resolves to, one binary column as `{ descriptor, payload }` (a Uint8Array). A later `apply` with a new revision updates the scene in place, keeping what did not change. `send(message)`, given to the constructor, receives what the browser would send Python: status, events, input values, selections and drag offsets. `command({ command, target, args })` runs the commands Python's async methods send (`settled`, `export_png`, `export_svg`, `camera`, `viewport`, `time`, `selection`, ...) and resolves to their results.

The scene format and the commands are python/PROTOCOL.md's; a scene names only components in `sceneRegistry`, and a protocol version other than its own is an error. Call `initializePlot()` before the first `apply`, and `dispose()` when the scene goes away. Setting `runtime.snapshot` to `{ src, alt, width, height, note }` shows that image, with the note, in the scene's place, as the notebook widget does in a browser without WebGPU.

## hmplot/templates

Page: /reference/svelte/package-templates.md

Render a code-free Python template inside a Svelte plot or data context.

### Example

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
  import { PortableTemplate } from "hmplot/templates";
  import trend from "./trend.hmplot.json";
</script>

<Plot data={table}>
  <PortableTemplate definition={trend} params={{ x: "day", y: "value" }} />
</Plot>
```

### Exports

- `PortableTemplate` (`component`): Renders an exported Python Template subtree inside the current Svelte HMPlot context; definition is its JSON file, params bind its named values, props are its main part's props (its contract's main, else its only mark; visible alone for a group of marks), or under a contract part's name an object of that part's props, events binds host callbacks by contract part name or unique node name, and children fill its slot.

### Usage

`hmplot/templates` publicly exports `PortableTemplate`, the Svelte loader for an exported
Python template. The repository's JavaScript `defineTemplate` and `TemplateHost` are internal
authoring tools, not exports of this package entry. Use an ordinary Svelte component for a
pattern authored directly in an application.

A portable file is an expanded component tree: it can hold marks inside a host Plot, or a
non-mark pattern such as Calculate → Plot → slot inside a host Data scope. Supply the table
from the host. The same file loads in Python with `hm.load_template(path)`.

| Prop | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `definition` | The exported `.hmplot.json` object, not a JavaScript template definition. |
| `params` | The file's explicit parameter values; omitted values use marker defaults. Unknown or missing required parameters are errors. |
| `props` | Extra properties for the main mark, or a named-part object such as `{band: {opacity: 0.2}}`. A group with several marks and no main takes only `visible` besides named-part overrides. |
| `events` | Host callbacks by contract part name, else a node's unique `name`, such as `{head: {click: handler}}`. They are not code from the file. |
| Children | A Svelte snippet placed at the exported slot; supplying children without a slot is an error. |

Each instance remaps node IDs and has its own children and handlers. Changing `params` or
`props` updates its instantiated tree; it does not run Python. Main/named parts, nested
contracts, follower visibility and legend entries retain their declared behavior. Slot
children remain the caller's marks and do not select the template's main part.

Python authors with `hm.Template` or `@hm.template`, passes explicit `hm.template_param()`
markers, then exports an instance with an empty slot and no registered callbacks. A marker's
own JSON default, not the Python function's default, determines whether a file parameter is
optional. Attach Python callbacks after loading, or Svelte callbacks through `events`.
Python methods and attributes do not travel.

Files require a matching HMPlot version and are limited to 1 MiB, 256 nodes and 32 nesting
levels. Loaders reject embedded resources, external URLs, unsupported component properties
and callbacks in the file. See [Template](template) and the
repository's `docs/PORTABLE-TEMPLATES.md` authoring guide for mark composition, a non-mark
transform/layout pattern, complete programs and exact limits.
Templates compose existing behavior; [plug-ins](/HMPlot/reference/svelte/plugins.md) supply new execution or rendering.

Download and adapt [candlestick](/HMPlot/examples/template-candlestick.md),
[parallel coordinates](/HMPlot/examples/template-parallel.md), [ridgeline](/HMPlot/examples/template-ridgeline.md),
and [radar](/HMPlot/examples/template-radar.md). Each provides Python authoring/loading, Svelte loading,
a portable JSON file and its host-data shape.

## hmplot/types

Page: /reference/svelte/package-types.md

Option types for settings a component registers: a default, a settings-pane control and a conversion.

### Example

```svelte
<script>
  // A pattern's settings, shown in the settings pane (see hmplot/compound).
  import { composition } from "hmplot/compound";
  import { IntegerType, SelectType } from "hmplot/types";
  let { name = undefined } = $props();
  const options = composition.getOptionsContext().splitUnique(name, "group", "Strip");
  composition.setOptionsContext(options);
  options.ensure("stripBins", new IntegerType({ defaultValue: 20, min: 1, max: 100 }));
  options.ensure("stripScale", new SelectType({ defaultValue: "count", options: ["count", "density"] }));
</script>
```

### Exports

- `FieldType` (`class`): The base type. params: defaultValue, label (default from the name), transform (value conversion) and ui (the pane's control spec, or false for none).
- `ScalarType` (`class`): A number: params min, max and step; a slider (0 to 1 by 0.01 unless given).
- `IntegerType` (`class`): A ScalarType rounded to an integer; step 1.
- `CountType` (`class`): An IntegerType from 0 to 100,000.
- `ValueType` (`class`): A ScalarType from 0 to 1.
- `OpacityType` (`class`): A ScalarType from 0 to 1, default 1.
- `WidthType` (`class`): A ScalarType from 0 to 20 by 0.1, default 1.
- `BooleanType` (`class`): true or false, default false; a checkbox.
- `SelectType` (`class`): One of params.options; a select.
- `ColormapType` (`class`): A colormap name (default Viridis).
- `ShapeType` (`class`): A point shape name (default circle), the registered shapes included.
- `Shape3DType` (`class`): "sphere" (default) or "cube".
- `TransformType` (`class`): A scale transform: linear (default), log, sqrt or symlog.
- `VectorType` (`class`): A vector of params.dimensions numbers.
- `Vector2Type` (`class`): A VectorType of 2.
- `Vector3Type` (`class`): A VectorType of 3.
- `Vector4Type` (`class`): A VectorType of 4.
- `PositionType` (`class`): A 3D position, default [0, 0, 0].
- `SizeType` (`class`): A size from 1 to 100, default 1.
- `RangeType` (`class`): A [min, max] pair, default [-1, 1]; an interval slider.
- `BoundsType` (`class`): A RangeType for an extent.
- `ColorType` (`class`): A CSS color, default white; a color picker.
- `FillType` (`class`): A fill color, default steelblue.
- `TypeRegistry` (`object`): The types by name: boolean, bounds, color, colormap, count, fill, integer, opacity, position, range, scalar, shape, shape3d, size, transform, value, vector2, vector3, vector4 and width.
- `createType(type, params)` (`FieldType`): A type from its registry name or class with params; a FieldType passes through. An unknown name is an error.

### Usage

A component's settings (what its settings pane edits, and what Python's `update()` and theme defaults reach) are registered on an options node: `options.ensure(name, type)` names a setting and gives it a type, whose `defaultValue` is its value until something sets it, whose `ui` is the pane's control (a slider, checkbox, select, color picker or text field) and whose `transform` converts what the pane sends. A pattern written in Svelte registers its settings this way, through `getOptionsContext()` and `setOptionsContext()` from [hmplot/compound](package-compound)'s `composition`; `composition` exports `IntegerType`, `SelectType` and `FieldType` too.

The constructor's params are `defaultValue`, `label` (default: from the setting's name), `ui` (an object merged into the control's spec, or `false` for no control) and `transform`; the numeric types also take `min`, `max` and `step`, and `SelectType` takes `options`. The types' other members (the GPU nodes a setting feeds, its uniform type) are internal to the marks and may change.

## stats

Page: /reference/python/package-stats.md

Statistical transform patterns; hm.stats in Python.

### Usage

Bin, Hexbin, Normalize, Window and Summary live in `hmplot/stats` in Svelte and `hm.stats`
in Python. They transform the data inherited by their children. Core operations such as
Calculate, Group, Filter and Sort stay in `hmplot`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot, Points } from "hmplot";
  import { Normalize } from "hmplot/stats";
</script>
<Plot data={{ x: [1, 2, 3] }}>
  <Normalize field="x"><Points x="x" y="normalized" /></Normalize>
</Plot>
```

```python
import hmplot as hm
with hm.Plot(data={"x": [1, 2, 3]}) as plot:
    with hm.stats.Normalize(field="x"):
        hm.Points(x="x", y="normalized")
```

Python's old root names raise an error naming the replacement. In Svelte, change the import
module; component props and child markup use the same spelling.

### Related examples

- [Histogram bins](/HMPlot/examples/histograms.md)

## charts

Page: /reference/python/package-charts.md

Chart patterns composed from core marks and transforms; hm.charts in Python.

### Usage

Chart patterns live in `hmplot/charts` in Svelte and `hm.charts` in Python. They compose the
core marks and transforms; use their reference pages to choose a pattern and its options.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
  import { Bar } from "hmplot/charts";
</script>
<Plot data={{ category: ["A", "B"], value: [2, 3] }}>
  <Bar x="category" y="value" />
</Plot>
```

```python
import hmplot as hm
with hm.Plot(data={"category": ["A", "B"], "value": [2, 3]}) as plot:
    hm.charts.Bar(x="category", y="value")
```

The catalog includes Bar, Histogram, BoxPlot, Violin, Swarm, Pie, Lollipop, Smooth, Ecdf,
DensityContour, DensityBands, RuleX, RuleY, Callout, Crosshair, ErrorBars and Arrows.
Python's old root names raise an error naming the replacement; Svelte imports must use the
charts module. Core marks such as Points, Line, Rect, Text and Segments stay in `hmplot`.

### Building blocks

| Pattern | Composition |
| --- | --- |
| Bar | BarGeometry transform and Prism |
| Histogram | Bin transform and Rect; a hidden Points part supplies brushing |
| BoxPlot | BoxStats and BoxOutliers transforms, Rect, Segments and Points |
| Violin | Density, Area and Anchor |
| Swarm | Dodge and Points |
| Pie | PieGeometry, Rect and a polar Frame |
| Lollipop | BarGeometry, Segments and Points |
| Smooth | Regression, Area and Line |
| Ecdf | Empirical-distribution transform and a step Line |
| DensityContour | Density, Contour and Segments |
| DensityBands | Density, Contour, Filter and Polygon |
| RuleX, RuleY | Segments placed at the frame edges |
| Callout | Text with a box and leader |
| Crosshair | Segments and Text, driven by the pointer |
| ErrorBars | Segments with bar caps |
| Arrows | Directed segments with arrowheads |

### Related examples

- [Bar chart](/HMPlot/examples/bar.md)
- [Histogram bins](/HMPlot/examples/histograms.md)

## hmplot/compound

Page: /reference/svelte/package-compound.md

The built-in templates, and the experimental surface to write your own patterns.

### Example

```svelte
import { Lollipop, composition } from "hmplot/compound";
const { ErrorBars, Points, ThemeDefaults, minimum, maximum } = composition;
```

### Exports

- `Histogram, Violin, BoxPlot, Swarm, Bar, Lollipop, Pie, RuleX, RuleY, Crosshair, Callout, Smooth, Ecdf, DensityContour, DensityBands, ErrorBars` (`components`): The built-in templates, the same components as hmplot/charts (each has its reference page), and their props types.
- `composition` (`namespace (experimental)`): What a pattern written in Svelte is built from: Transform, DataBoundary, ThemeDefaults, the options and data contexts, the data-bound primitive marks, the transforms the built-in templates wrap, framePointer and planeRule, expression builders and the input helpers. Names and behavior may change in any release.

### Usage

The built-in templates, built from transforms and simpler marks, are exported from `hmplot/charts` (`hm.charts` in Python). `hmplot/compound` adds `composition`, everything a pattern written in Svelte may use: the `Transform` component that runs a named transform around its children, `DataBoundary`, `ThemeDefaults`, `Undescribed` (a helper part left out of the plot's description), the options and data contexts, the data-bound primitive marks (Rect, Points, Line, ErrorBars, Polygon, ...), the transforms the built-in templates wrap, `planeRule` and `framePointer`, and expression and input helpers.

`composition` is **experimental**: its names and behavior may change in any release, unlike the rest of the package. Its complete list, with what each part is for, a worked Lollipop and the conventions a pattern written in Svelte follows (forward the remaining props to the mark that carries color and interaction, re-export `getLegendSource` and `getMark`, give secondary parts `legend={false}`), is in docs/USAGE.md, "Writing a pattern". In Python a [template](template) packages a pattern of existing components.

### Related examples

- [Lollipop chart](/HMPlot/examples/lollipop.md)

## charts.Marginals

Page: /reference/python/marginals.md

A scatter plot with a histogram of each of its columns along its top and right sides.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {
    "height": [151, 156, 158, 160, 162, 163, 165, 166, 168, 169, 170, 171, 172, 174, 175, 176, 178, 180, 182, 185],
    "weight": [48, 52, 55, 54, 58, 61, 59, 63, 62, 66, 65, 70, 68, 72, 71, 75, 74, 79, 83, 86],
}
figure = hm.charts.Marginals(data=data, x="height", y="weight", bins=8, height=360)
figure
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Marginals } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = {
    height: [151, 156, 158, 160, 162, 163, 165, 166, 168, 169, 170, 171, 172, 174, 175, 176, 178, 180, 182, 185],
    weight: [48, 52, 55, 54, 58, 61, 59, 63, 62, 66, 65, 70, 68, 72, 71, 75, 74, 79, 83, 86],
  };
</script>

<Marginals {data} x="height" y="weight" bins={8} height={360} />
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `data` (`table`): A table or live pipeline output for the scatter and its histograms; the same as wrapping the Marginals in Data.
- `schema` (`object`): Column types for data, such as {"day": "datetime"}, as on Data.
- `key` (`column | column[]`): The column, or columns, that identify each row of data across updates, as on Data.
- `bins` (`number | number[] | "auto" | "sturges" | "fd" | "scott" | expression`): Both histograms' bins, as Histogram's bins: a count, edges, a rule or an expression. Default: `30`.
- `height` (`number`): The height of the whole figure, at least 160: the histograms take a fifth of it (at least 48 px) across the scatter's side, and the scatter the rest. Default: `450` px.
- `viewport` (`{x, y, zoom, zoomX, zoomY, center}`): The scatter's 2D view, as a Plot's viewport; the histograms follow it on their axes.

#### Position

- `x` (`column`): The column the scatter plots along x, binned by the histogram above it. Required.
- `y` (`column`): The column the scatter plots along y, binned by the histogram to its right. Required.

#### Appearance

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill`, `color`, `size`, `opacity`, `outline_color`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `brush`, `nearby`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `drag`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Symbol

- `shape` (`string | column | string[]`): The point symbol: a shape name, a column of categories mapped to shapes, or one name per row. Default: `"circle"`.
- `shape_scale` (`scale`): A categorical() scale from the shape column's categories to shape names.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

### Usage

Marginals draws a scatter of `x` against `y` with a histogram of `x` above it and one of `y` to its right, as seaborn's jointplot draws it: three Plots whose plot areas line up, each histogram sharing the scatter's domain on its axis and following it as the scatter pans and zooms. The histograms take a fifth of `height` (at least 48 px) and have no axes of their own; `bins` sets both.

Its other props go to the scatter's Points: `fill="species"` colors the points by a column (with the scatter's legend), `size`, `opacity`, `tooltip` and `brush` work as on Points. Its children are drawn in the scatter's Plot, over the points (a Smooth, rules, labels). Give the rows with `data`, or put the Marginals in a Data. It sits where a Plot does: in a Scene, Row, Column or Grid, not inside a Plot. Its PNG, SVG and PDF exports compose its three views; bound in Svelte, `view("top")`, `view("main")` and `view("right")` give each view's Plot handle.

Marginals is a chart template, built from Plots, Points and Histograms: import it from `hmplot/charts` in JavaScript or use `hm.charts.Marginals` in Python. Its panels fill their grid cells in both live views and image exports.

See the executable [marginal distributions recipe](/HMPlot/recipes.md#scatter-with-marginal-distributions) for human-readable axis labels and category colors. The histogram count axes fit their counts automatically. Do not pin a count domain to `[0, 1]` unless the histogram is normalized to that range; raw counts would clip into solid blocks. Use Marginals rather than manually aligning a Row and Column of plots.

`hm.check(chart)` reports the scatter and both histograms together, including their diagnostics and the composed figure PNG.

## charts.FocusContext

Page: /reference/python/focus-context.md

A line chart over a strip of the whole series: dragging across the strip zooms the chart to that x interval.

### Example

```python
import math
import hmplot as hm

days = list(range(365))
data = {"day": days, "visits": [200 + 80 * math.sin(d / 9) + d / 2 for d in days]}
## Drag across the strip below to zoom the chart to those days; clear the brush to see them all.
chart = hm.charts.FocusContext(data=data, x="day", y="visits", height=360)
chart
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { FocusContext } from "hmplot/charts";
  const days = Array.from({ length: 365 }, (_, d) => d);
  const data = { day: days, visits: days.map((d) => 200 + 80 * Math.sin(d / 9) + d / 2) };
</script>

<!-- Drag across the strip below to zoom the chart to those days; clear the brush to see them all. -->
<FocusContext {data} x="day" y="visits" height={360} />
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `data` (`table`): A table or live pipeline output for both views; the same as wrapping the FocusContext in Data.
- `schema` (`object`): Column types for data, such as {"day": "datetime"}, as on Data.
- `key` (`column | column[]`): The column, or columns, that identify each row of data across updates, as on Data.
- `height` (`number`): The height of the whole figure, at least 160: the strip takes a fifth of it (at least 48 px), the chart the rest. Default: `360` px.
- `viewport` (`{x, y, zoom, zoomX, zoomY, center}`): The chart's 2D view, as a Plot's viewport.

#### Position

- `x` (`column`): The column the lines plot along x: a drag across the strip below zooms the chart to an interval of it (its brush's bounds), and clearing the brush shows it all. Required.
- `y` (`column`): The column the lines plot along y. Required.

#### Appearance

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill`, `color`, `size`, `width`, `opacity`, `outline_color`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `width_scale`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearby`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `drag`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Series

- `series` (`column | column[] | array`): Split the rows into separate paths, one per value of this column (Line, Area). Without it, a Line colored or an Area filled by a category column splits by that column.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

### Usage

FocusContext draws a line chart over a strip of the whole series, as overview-and-detail charts do: a drag across the strip brushes an interval of `x`, and the chart above shows that interval; clearing the brush (Escape, or its clear control) shows the whole series again. The two Plots' plot areas line up; the strip takes a fifth of `height` (at least 48 px) and has no y axis. The strip does not pan or zoom, so a plain drag brushes it.

Its other props go to the chart's Line: `series="ticker"` and `color="ticker"` draw a line per ticker in both views, `width`, `opacity` and `tooltip` work as on Line. Its children are drawn in the chart, over the lines (rules, labels, an [EndLabels](end-labels)). Give the rows with `data`, or put the FocusContext in a Data. It sits where a Plot does: in a Scene, Row, Column or Grid, not inside a Plot. Its PNG, SVG and PDF exports compose both views; bound in Svelte, `view("main")` and `view("context")` give each view's Plot handle.

FocusContext is a chart template, built from Plots and Lines: import it from `hmplot/charts` in JavaScript or use `hm.charts.FocusContext` in Python. The chart's x domain is the brush's bounds read from the data (`@brush_min:x` and `@brush_max:x` as a domain, see [Plot](plot)): the same composition works by hand for other marks.

## charts.Arrows

Page: /reference/python/arrows.md

Arrows from start to end, one per row, with heads sized in pixels.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

## One arrow per row, from its start to its end.
start = [[0, 0], [2, 3], [4, 1]]
end = [[1.5, 2], [3.5, 3], [3, 0]]
with hm.Plot(height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.Arrows(start=start, end=end)
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
import { Arrows } from "hmplot/charts";
  // One arrow per row, from its start to its end.
  const start = [[0, 0], [2, 3], [4, 1]];
  const end = [[1.5, 2], [3.5, 3], [3, 0]];
</script>

<Plot height={300} axes2d autoBounds>
  <Arrows {start} {end} />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `connections` (`connect()`): Draw between other marks instead of from start and end: connect(a, b, {key}) draws an arrow from a to b for each matched key.
- `curve` (`"linear" | "step" | "step-before" | "step-after" | "link-horizontal" | "link-vertical" | "quadratic" | "cubic"`): How each arrow runs from start to end; the head follows the curve. Default: `"linear"`.
- `control1` (`channel`): Each arrow's control point for a quadratic or cubic curve: a column of positions or an N x 2 (N x 3) array.
- `control2` (`channel`): Each arrow's second control point for a cubic curve.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Appearance

- `color` (`channel`): The line or text color: a CSS color, or a column mapped to colors. Default: the theme's (#3478c7 in the default theme).
- `width` (`channel`): The line width: a number, or a column mapped to widths. Default: the theme's (2 in the default theme). In px.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `opacity`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `color_scale`, `colormap`, `width_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `rows`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Segment ends

- `start` (`channel`): Where each segment starts (Segments, Arrows): a column of positions or an N x 2 (N x 3) array.
- `end` (`channel`): Where each segment ends, as start.

#### Map paths

- `interpolation` (`"great-circle" | "angular" | "cartesian"`): How a path between two points runs on a map or a globe: along a great circle, straight in longitude and latitude, or straight in space. Default: `"great-circle"`.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Shading

- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Arrowheads

- `head_length` (`number`, setting): The arrowhead's length. Default: `10` px.
- `head_width` (`number`, setting): The arrowhead's width. Default: `8` px.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

Import Arrows from `hmplot/charts` in Svelte; use `hm.charts.Arrows` in Python.

Default width is 2px; head length 10px and head width 8px. Each row is one arrow from its start to its end: the shaft stops where the head begins, and the head ends at the end point. Heads follow the displayed endpoint tangent on curved paths. Zero-length arrows are omitted; short paths clamp head length.

Arrows is a chart template over `Segments(cap="arrow")`, sharing its curves, filtering and interaction. Use Segments directly when you also need dashed shafts, a width scale or another cap style. Arrows keeps widths in CSS pixels, including width columns. Screen-sized arrows are unlit; use Arrows3D for lit solid geometry.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Vector, except** in a 3D view that holds a mark with no vector form there (Points3D, Surface or another 3D mark, a Heatmap or Image, a lit or additive mark, a globe or polar frame): then SVG and PDF exports draw all of that view's marks as one image, and `mode="vector"` refuses it. In other 3D views the arrows are vectors too, drawn back to front by depth (approximate where marks cross closely). A `color` column and a `curve` stay vector. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

#### Connections

With `connections={connect(before, after, {key})}` Arrows draw one screen-sized arrow per matched key from the earlier endpoint to the later one, as in the before/after gallery example. See [connect()](connect).

### Related examples

- [Rooted tree](/HMPlot/examples/rooted-tree.md)

## charts.Bar

Page: /reference/python/bar.md

Bars from a baseline to a value, one per row, on a categorical axis.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"group": ["A", "B", "C", "D"], "total": [5, 8, 4, 7]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.Bar(x="group", y="total")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
import { Bar } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { group: ["A", "B", "C", "D"], total: [5, 8, 4, 7] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <Bar x="group" y="total" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `orientation` (`"horizontal" | "vertical"`): Vertical bars rise from categories on x; horizontal bars run from categories on y. Default: from which of x and y is categorical.
- `baseline` (`channel`): Where each bar starts on the value axis: a number or a column. Default: `0`.
- `band_fraction` (`number`): The share of its category's band each bar fills, 0 to 1; on a numeric axis, the bar's width in data units. Default: `0.8`.
- `arrange` (`"stack" | "group" | "overlap"`): Bars that share a category: "stack" stacks them from zero in the order of the column fill (or color) names, "group" sets them side by side with each fill value in the same slot of every category, "overlap" draws each from its baseline. One bar per category draws the same in all three. Default: "stack" ("overlap" with a baseline).
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`channel`): The categories along x for vertical bars, or the values the bars reach for horizontal ones.
- `y` (`channel`): The values the bars reach for vertical bars, or the categories along y for horizontal ones.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `z`, `position`.

#### Appearance

- `fill` (`channel`): The fill color: a CSS color, or a column of numbers or categories mapped to colors. Default: the theme's first palette color (#3478c7 in the default theme).

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `color`, `size`, `opacity`, `outline_color`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Symbol rotation

- `rotation` (`number`): The symbol's rotation. Default: `0` degrees.

#### Symbol

- `shape` (`string | column | string[]`): The point symbol: a shape name, a column of categories mapped to shapes, or one name per row. Default: `"circle"`.
- `shape_scale` (`scale`): A categorical() scale from the shape column's categories to shape names.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Shading

- `lit` (`boolean`, setting): Shade the mark with the plot's lights. Default: `False`.
- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

Defaults to zero baseline and 80% categorical band width. Orientation follows the categorical axis unless supplied; string and boolean literals infer the same orientation as categorical columns.

For linked aggregate bars, see the [click drilldown recipe](/HMPlot/recipes.md): preserve source rows, Group each branch, and Filter before the target Group.

Bars that share a category stack by default (`arrange="stack"`), from zero, in the order of the column `fill` (or `color`) names: positive values up, negative down. `arrange="group"` sets them side by side, each `fill` value in the same slot of every category, the slots sharing the band; `arrange="overlap"` draws each from its baseline. A Bar with a `baseline` overlaps unless told otherwise. Aggregation is explicit: use Group before Bar to total rows. Grouping moves each bar with `xOffset` (or `yOffset`), which Points, Prism and Text take too: a position offset in data units, so one band of a categorical axis.

Bar is a built-in template, built from transforms and simpler marks: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Vector, except** in a 3D view that holds a mark with no vector form there (Points3D, Surface or another 3D mark, a Heatmap or Image, a lit or additive mark, a globe or polar frame): then SVG and PDF exports draw all of that view's marks as one image, and `mode="vector"` refuses it. In other 3D views the bars are vectors too, drawn back to front by depth (approximate where marks cross closely). A `fill` column (numbers or categories, as stacked or grouped bars have) stays vector. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

### Related examples

- [Bar chart](/HMPlot/examples/bar.md)

## charts.BoxPlot

Page: /reference/python/box-plot.md

Box-and-whisker plots: each group's quartiles, median, whiskers and outliers.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {
    "group": ["A", "A", "A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C", "C", "C"],
    "value": [2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 3.8, 5.2, 4.4, 5.1, 5.6, 6.3, 9.8, 3.1, 3.5, 3.9, 4.1, 4.6],
}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.BoxPlot(x="group", y="value")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
import { BoxPlot } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = {
    group: ["A", "A", "A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C", "C", "C"],
    value: [2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 3.8, 5.2, 4.4, 5.1, 5.6, 6.3, 9.8, 3.1, 3.5, 3.9, 4.1, 4.6],
  };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <BoxPlot x="group" y="value" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `orientation` (`"horizontal" | "vertical"`): Vertical boxes stand on categories along x; horizontal boxes sit on categories along y. Default: from which of x and y is categorical.
- `band_fraction` (`number`): The share of its category's band each box fills, 0 to 1; on a numeric axis, the box's width in data units. Default: `0.8`.
- `whisker` (`number`): How far the whiskers may reach beyond the box, in interquartile ranges; each ends at the farthest value within that reach (Tukey's rule). Default: `1.5`.
- `outliers` (`boolean`): Draw the values beyond the whiskers as points. Default: `True`.
- `outlier_size` (`number`): The outlier points' diameter. Default: `2.5` px.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`channel`): The groups along x, a box each, or the measurements for horizontal boxes.
- `y` (`channel`): The measurements for vertical boxes, or the groups along y for horizontal ones.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `z`, `position`.

#### Appearance

- `fill` (`channel`): The boxes' and outliers' fill: a CSS color, or the group column to color each group. Default: `"#547ba2"`.
- `outline_color` (`channel`): The whiskers' and medians' color, and the boxes' outline color when outline_width is set. Default: `"#30343b"`.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `color`, `size`, `opacity`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Symbol rotation

- `rotation` (`number`): The symbol's rotation. Default: `0` degrees.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Geometry

- `detail` (`number`, setting): How finely a point's or a surface's geometry is divided (sphere segments, grid cells).

#### Shading

- `lit` (`boolean`, setting): Shade the mark with the plot's lights. Default: `False`.
- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

Uses Tukey whiskers at 1.5×IQR by default. Outliers retain source observation identities. Configure orientation, box width, whisker multiplier, outlier visibility/size, fill, and outline.

BoxPlot is a built-in template (TODO 130.3): BoxStats places each box, whisker and median, drawn by a Rect and two Segments, and BoxOutliers keeps the rows past the whiskers, drawn as Points. Import it from `hmplot/charts`.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Vector, except** in a 3D view that holds a mark with no vector form there (Points3D, Surface or another 3D mark, a Heatmap or Image, a lit or additive mark, a globe or polar frame): then SVG and PDF exports draw all of that view's marks as one image, and `mode="vector"` refuses it. In other 3D views the boxes and whiskers are vectors too, drawn back to front by depth (approximate where marks cross closely). A `fill` column stays vector. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

### Related examples

- [Box plot](/HMPlot/examples/box-plot.md)

## charts.Callout

Page: /reference/python/callout.md

A note a fixed distance from a point, with a leader line to the point.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"x": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], "y": [3, 4, 2, 5, 6, 5]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.Line(x="x", y="y")
    hm.charts.Callout(x=5, y=6, text="Peak")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot, Line } from "hmplot";
import { Callout } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { x: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], y: [3, 4, 2, 5, 6, 5] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <Line x="x" y="y" />
  <Callout x={5} y={6} text="Peak" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `text` (`string | number | column | (string | number)[]`): The text: a string or a number, or a column of them for a callout per row.
- `dx` (`channel`): How far right of its point the text sits (left when negative): a number or a column. Default: `24` px.
- `dy` (`channel`): How far below its point the text sits (above when negative): a number or a column. Default: `-24` px.
- `box` (`boolean | {fill, outlineColor, outlineWidth, padding, radius, opacity}`): A box behind the text: true for white with a gray outline, or its style. Without one the text has a halo of the plot's background. Default: `False`.
- `leader` (`boolean | {color, width}`): The line from near the point to the text (or its box): true (1.5 px in the text's color), false, or its color and width. Default: `True`.
- `align` (`"left" | "center" | "right" | "auto"`): How the text sits at its offset; "auto" puts each row's text on the side of the point it is offset to. Default: `"auto"`.
- `font` (`string`): The text's font, a CSS font-family. Default: the plot's font.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`channel`): The x of the point the callout points at: a number or a time draws one callout, a column one per row.
- `y` (`channel`): The y of the point the callout points at.

#### Appearance

- `color` (`channel`): The text's color: a CSS color, or a column mapped to colors. Default: the theme's text color, as Text's.
- `size` (`channel`): The text's font size: a number, or a column mapped to sizes. Default: the theme's font size, as Text's (14 in the default theme). In px.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill`, `width`, `opacity`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `width_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

- `legend` (`boolean`): Whether the mark has a legend entry. Default: `False`.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `visible`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

Glyph outlines are not supported. Style the border of a label box with `box={...}`.

A Callout points at a value with a note a fixed distance away: `dx` and `dy` pixels from its point (right and down; the default is up and to the right), with a leader line from just short of the point to the text. The text has no box: it is drawn over a halo of the plot's background, so it reads over the data; `box` puts it in one (white with a gray outline by default), and the leader then ends at the box's nearest edge. The leader is 1.5 px in the text's color unless `leader` sets its own. The text takes the theme's size and color, as Text does, the size rule and band labels use too. Numbers and times for `x` and `y` draw one callout; columns draw one per row, and `dx`, `dy` and `text` may be columns too. The text aligns to the side of the point it sits on (`align="auto"`), row by row when `dx` is a column.

Callouts do not move to avoid each other or the data: choose the offsets. It is a Text with a leader, so Text takes `box` and `leader` as well, and exports draw the leader, the box or the halo, and the text as vectors, the text searchable.

Callout is a built-in template, built from transforms and simpler marks: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

### Related examples

- [Titles, bands and callouts](/HMPlot/examples/annotations.md)

## charts.Crosshair

Page: /reference/python/crosshair.md

Rules that follow the pointer across the frame, with a readout of its x and y.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"x": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], "y": [3, 4, 2, 5, 6, 5]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.Line(x="x", y="y")
    hm.charts.Crosshair()
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot, Line } from "hmplot";
import { Crosshair } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { x: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], y: [3, 4, 2, 5, 6, 5] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <Line x="x" y="y" />
  <Crosshair />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

- `axes` (`"x" | "y" | "xy"`): Which rules to draw: a vertical one ("x"), a horizontal one ("y"), or both. Default: `"xy"`.
- `readout` (`boolean`): Show the pointer's value on each axis, finer than the ticks, where readout_position puts it. Default: `True`.
- `readout_position` (`"edges" | "pointer"`): Where the readouts sit: just inside the frame's bottom (x) and left (y) edges, or as one label beside the pointer, for a polar frame or a map, whose rules have no edge to pin to. Default: `"edges"`.
- `color` (`color`): The rules' color. Default: `"#40505d"`.
- `width` (`number`): The rules' width. Default: `1` px.
- `dash` (`boolean | number | [number, number]`): Dash the rules: true (4 px dashes and gaps), a dash length (gaps as long), or [dash, gap], measured along the drawn rules. In px.
- `text_color` (`color`): The readouts' text color. Default: `"#40505d"`.
- `name` (`string`): The rules' name in the settings pane.

### Usage

Place a Crosshair in a Plot (or in a Frame) and it follows the pointer there: a rule each way and a readout of each value. Readouts are finer than the ticks: a time with its time of day, a number to about a thousandth of the visible span, angles and map coordinates in degrees. By default they sit just inside the frame's bottom and left edges; `readoutPosition="pointer"` puts one label beside the pointer that holds both, for a polar frame or a map, whose rules have no edge to pin to.

Nothing draws while the pointer is off the frame. A still pointer costs nothing: the rules and readouts update once per animation frame with a move. `axes="x"` keeps only the vertical rule; `readout={false}` drops the text.

Crosshair is a built-in template, built from transforms and simpler marks: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Left out.** PNG, SVG and PDF exports leave the crosshair out: it draws only where the pointer is. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

### Related examples

- [Crosshair and rules](/HMPlot/examples/crosshair.md)

## charts.DensityBands

Page: /reference/python/density-bands.md

Filled bands of the density of points in two dimensions, each filled by its lower level.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"x": [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5], "y": [2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 4]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.DensityBands(x="x", y="y")
    hm.Points(x="x", y="y")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot, Points } from "hmplot";
import { DensityBands } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { x: [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5], y: [2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 4] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <DensityBands x="x" y="y" />
  <Points x="x" y="y" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `weight` (`column`): A column of nonnegative weights, one per row; without it every row counts once.
- `bandwidth` (`number | [number, number] | "auto"`): The width of the Gaussian kernel: one for both axes, one per axis, or "auto" for Scott's rule. Default: `"auto"`. In data units.
- `resolution` (`number | [number, number]`): The size of the grid the density is estimated on: [along x, along y], or one number for both. Default: `128`.
- `bounds` (`{x: [number, number], y: [number, number]}`): The region the density is estimated over. Default: the points' extent, widened by three bandwidths. In data units.
- `thresholds` (`number | number[]`): How many band edges, chosen as round values over the density's range, or the edges themselves. Default: `10`.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`column`): The column along x of the points whose density is banded.
- `y` (`column`): The column along y of the points whose density is banded.

#### Appearance

- `fill` (`channel`): The bands' fill: a CSS color, or lower (the density at the band's lower edge) mapped to colors. Default: each band's lower level.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `opacity`, `outline_color`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `colormap`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Shading

- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

### Usage

Density, Contour, then Polygon filled by each band's lower level, as d3's contourDensity draws its filled bands. The first band (from the least density up) covers the whole grid, so it is left out. For contour lines use [DensityContour](/HMPlot/reference/svelte/density-contour.md); to show both, draw both.

DensityBands is a built-in template, built from transforms and simpler marks: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Vector, except** in a 3D view that holds a mark with no vector form there (Points3D, Surface or another 3D mark, a Heatmap or Image, a lit or additive mark, a globe or polar frame): then SVG and PDF exports draw all of that view's marks as one image, and `mode="vector"` refuses it. In other 3D views the bands are vectors too, drawn back to front by depth (approximate where marks cross closely). Filled by level (the default) they stay vector. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

Band outlines follow the level boundaries, excluding internal cell and triangulation edges.

### Related examples

- [Density contours](/HMPlot/examples/density-contours.md)

## charts.DensityContour

Page: /reference/python/density-contour.md

Contour lines of the density of points in two dimensions.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"x": [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5], "y": [2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 4]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.DensityContour(x="x", y="y")
    hm.Points(x="x", y="y")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot, Points } from "hmplot";
import { DensityContour } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { x: [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5], y: [2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 4] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <DensityContour x="x" y="y" />
  <Points x="x" y="y" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `weight` (`column`): A column of nonnegative weights, one per row; without it every row counts once.
- `bandwidth` (`number | [number, number] | "auto"`): The width of the Gaussian kernel: one for both axes, one per axis, or "auto" for Scott's rule. Default: `"auto"`. In data units.
- `resolution` (`number | [number, number]`): The size of the grid the density is estimated on: [along x, along y], or one number for both. Default: `128`.
- `bounds` (`{x: [number, number], y: [number, number]}`): The region the density is estimated over. Default: the points' extent, widened by three bandwidths. In data units.
- `thresholds` (`number | number[]`): How many contour levels, chosen as round values over the density's range, or the levels themselves. Default: `10`.
- `mode` (`"lines" | "bands"`): Deprecated: use DensityBands for filled bands; mode will be removed. "lines" draws contour lines, colored by their level; "bands" draws a DensityBands. Default: `"lines"`.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`column`): The column along x of the points whose density is contoured.
- `y` (`column`): The column along y of the points whose density is contoured.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `z`, `position`.

#### Appearance

- `fill` (`channel`): The bands' fill, with the deprecated mode="bands": a CSS color, or lower (the density at the band's lower edge) mapped to colors. Default: each band's lower level.
- `color` (`channel`): The lines' color: a CSS color, or level (the density along the line) mapped to colors. Default: each line's level.
- `width` (`channel`): The lines' width. Default: `1` px.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `size`, `opacity`, `outline_color`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `width_scale`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Map paths

- `interpolation` (`"great-circle" | "angular" | "cartesian"`): How a path between two points runs on a map or a globe: along a great circle, straight in longitude and latitude, or straight in space. Default: `"great-circle"`.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Shading

- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

Density, Contour, then Segments colored by level, as d3's contourDensity draws its lines. For filled bands use [DensityBands](/HMPlot/reference/svelte/density-bands.md). `mode="bands"` still draws a DensityBands, with a warning; it is deprecated and will be removed.

DensityContour is a built-in template, built from transforms and simpler marks: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Vector, except** in a 3D view that holds a mark with no vector form there (Points3D, Surface or another 3D mark, a Heatmap or Image, a lit or additive mark, a globe or polar frame): then SVG and PDF exports draw all of that view's marks as one image, and `mode="vector"` refuses it. In other 3D views the contours are vectors too, drawn back to front by depth (approximate where marks cross closely). Colored by level (the default) they stay vector. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

The lines take color, width and opacity; they have no second outline stroke.

### Related examples

- [Density contours](/HMPlot/examples/density-contours.md)

## charts.Ecdf

Page: /reference/python/ecdf-chart.md

Empirical cumulative distributions as step lines, one per group.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"value": [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.Ecdf(x="value")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
import { Ecdf } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { value: [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <Ecdf x="value" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `by` (`column`): Groups: a step line each, colored by its group.
- `complementary` (`boolean`): Draw the share of values above each value (1 − ECDF) instead of at or below it. Default: `False`.
- `normalize` (`"fraction" | "count"`): Measure in fractions of the group or in counts of rows. Default: `"fraction"`.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`column`): The column whose distribution is drawn.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `y`, `z`, `position`.

#### Appearance

- `color` (`channel`): The line or text color: a CSS color, or a column mapped to colors. Default: the by column, when given.
- `width` (`channel`): The line width: a number, or a column mapped to widths. Default: `2` px.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill`, `size`, `opacity`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `width_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Shading

- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `sampling` (`"random" | "uniform-x"`): Which rows a Line keeps when it has more than max_instances: a random sample, or the extremes across even steps of x. Default: `"random"`.
- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

Each group's rows in value order, each at the share of its group at or below it, drawn as a step Line per group, colored by it. A Legend with `channel="color"` lists the groups.

Ecdf is a built-in template, built from transforms and simpler marks: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Vector, except** in a 3D view that holds a mark with no vector form there (Points3D, Surface or another 3D mark, a Heatmap or Image, a lit or additive mark, a globe or polar frame): then SVG and PDF exports draw all of that view's marks as one image, and `mode="vector"` refuses it. In other 3D views the lines are vectors too, drawn back to front by depth (approximate where marks cross closely). With `by`, each group's line keeps its color. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

### Related examples

- [ECDFs by species](/HMPlot/examples/ecdf.md)

## charts.ErrorBars

Page: /reference/python/error-bars.md

Error bars: an interval with caps at each row, such as a confidence interval.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"x": [1, 2, 3, 4], "y": [3, 5, 4, 6], "lower": [2, 4, 3.5, 5], "upper": [4, 6, 4.5, 7]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.ErrorBars(x="x", y="y", lower="lower", upper="upper")
    hm.Points(x="x", y="y")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot, Points } from "hmplot";
import { ErrorBars } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { x: [1, 2, 3, 4], y: [3, 5, 4, 6], lower: [2, 4, 3.5, 5], upper: [4, 6, 4.5, 7] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <ErrorBars x="x" y="y" lower="lower" upper="upper" />
  <Points x="x" y="y" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `lower` (`channel`): Where each bar starts, in its axis's units (not a distance from the point).
- `upper` (`channel`): Where each bar ends, in its axis's units; a bar whose upper is below its lower is not drawn.
- `orientation` (`"vertical" | "horizontal"`): Whether the bars run along y or along x. Default: `"vertical"`.
- `cap_size` (`number`): The length of the caps across each bar's ends. Default: `6` px.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`channel`): Each bar's x position; horizontal bars run from lower to upper along x instead.
- `y` (`channel`): Each bar's y position; vertical bars run from lower to upper along y instead.
- `position` (`channel`): Each bar's point as one column of positions or an N x 2 (N x 3) array, instead of x and y.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `z`.

#### Appearance

- `color` (`channel`): The line or text color: a CSS color, or a column mapped to colors. Default: the theme's (#3478c7 in the default theme).
- `width` (`channel`): The line width: a number, or a column mapped to widths. Default: the theme's (1 in the default theme). In px.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `opacity`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `color_scale`, `colormap`, `width_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `rows`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Shading

- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

This mark has no separate outline channel. Use `color` and `width` for its line stroke.

Bars run along y (orientation="horizontal": along x) and caps default to 6px. lower and upper are absolute coordinates, not distances from the observation; a bar whose upper is below its lower, or with a bound missing, is not drawn and does not widen the axis. Each complete bar retains its source identity. Supports Cartesian 2D/3D, polar frames and 2D maps.

ErrorBars is a built-in template over [Segments](/HMPlot/reference/svelte/segments.md) with bar caps: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

> **SVG and PDF export**
>
> **Vector, except** in a 3D view that holds a mark with no vector form there (Points3D, Surface or another 3D mark, a Heatmap or Image, a lit or additive mark, a globe or polar frame): then SVG and PDF exports draw all of that view's marks as one image, and `mode="vector"` refuses it. In other 3D views the error bars are vectors too, drawn back to front by depth (approximate where marks cross closely). A `color` column of numbers or categories stays vector. See [what is not exported as vector](/HMPlot/docs/export.md).

### Related examples

- [Legends & uncertainty](/HMPlot/examples/guides.md)

## charts.Histogram

Page: /reference/python/histogram.md

Bars counting how many values fall in each bin of a numeric column.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"value": [1.2, 2.3, 2.8, 3.1, 3.4, 3.6, 3.9, 4.2, 4.5, 4.7, 5.1, 5.6, 6.4, 7.3]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.Histogram(x="value", bins=5)
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
import { Histogram } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = {
    value: [1.2, 2.3, 2.8, 3.1, 3.4, 3.6, 3.9, 4.2, 4.5, 4.7, 5.1, 5.6, 6.4, 7.3],
  };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <Histogram x="value" bins={5} />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `bins` (`number | number[] | "auto" | "sturges" | "fd" | "scott" | expression`): A bin count, the bins' edges, a rule that picks the count from the data (as numpy's does), or an expression such as power(count("x"), 0.5). Default: `30`.
- `normalization` (`"count" | "proportion" | "density"`): What each bar's length measures: its values ("count"), their share of all values ("proportion"), or that share divided by the bin's width ("density"). Default: `"count"`.
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`column | number[]`): The values to bin along x, for vertical bars: a column or per-row values. Give x or y, not both.
- `y` (`column | number[]`): The values to bin along y, for horizontal bars. Give x or y, not both.

#### Appearance

- `fill` (`channel`): The bars' fill: a CSS color, or a column of the bins (such as count) mapped to colors. Default: the theme's first palette color (#3478c7 in the default theme).

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `color`, `size`, `width`, `opacity`, `outline_color`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `width_scale`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

- `brush` (`boolean | {selection, axis}`): Shift-drag brushes an interval of the binned column along its axis (x, or y for a horizontal histogram): the rows in it are @brushed in every view of the data, so a Filter elsewhere follows it (a crossfilter). true, or {selection} for a named selection.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Symbol rotation

- `rotation` (`number`): The symbol's rotation. Default: `0` degrees.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Shading

- `lit` (`boolean`, setting): Shade the mark with the plot's lights. Default: `False`.
- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

Exactly one of x or y selects orientation. Defaults to 30 bins and count.

`brush` (`brush=True` in Python) lets a Shift-drag brush an interval of the binned column along its axis: the rows in it are `@brushed` in every view of the data, so a `Filter(where="@brushed")` around another mark follows it (a crossfilter), and `respond="brushed"` fades this histogram's other bins. `brush={ selection }` writes a named selection instead, for a crossfilter whose views each filter by the others' brushes. proportion divides by included observations; density also divides by bin width. Empty bins and zero on the count axis are included.

`bins` takes a count, explicit edges, a rule name (`"auto"`, `"sturges"`, `"fd"`, `"scott"`), or an expression such as `power(count("x"), 0.5)`, which the settings pane shows read-only. In a Facet, a rule or expression is resolved once over every cell, so the cells share their edges.

Histogram is a built-in template, built from transforms and simpler marks: import it from `hmplot/charts`.

### Related examples

- [Histogram bins](/HMPlot/examples/histograms.md)

## charts.Lollipop

Page: /reference/python/lollipop.md

A stem from a baseline to each value, with a point at its end.

### Example

```python
import hmplot as hm

data = {"category": ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"], "value": [18, 31, 12, 44, 26]}
with hm.Plot(data=data, height=300, axes2d=True) as plot:
    hm.charts.Lollipop(x="category", y="value")
plot
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Plot } from "hmplot";
import { Lollipop } from "hmplot/charts";
  const data = { category: ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"], value: [18, 31, 12, 44, 26] };
</script>

<Plot {data} height={300} axes2d>
  <Lollipop x="category" y="value" />
</Plot>
```

### Options

Keywords are snake_case.

#### Options

- `orientation` (`"horizontal" | "vertical"`): Whether the stems run along y ("vertical") or along x ("horizontal"). Default: horizontal when only y is categorical, else vertical.
- `baseline` (`channel`): Where the stems start: a number or a column. Values on either side of it get a stem. Default: `0`.
- `stem` (`object`): The stems' own Segments props, as one object: {color: "gray", width: 2, dash: [2, 2]}. Defaults to the Lollipop theme's color and width (#8a949e and 1.5 pixels).
- `data` (`table`): A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

#### Position

- `x` (`channel`): The categories along x for vertical stems, or the values the stems reach for horizontal ones.
- `y` (`channel`): The values the stems reach for vertical stems, or the categories along y for horizontal ones.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `z`, `position`.

#### Appearance

- `size` (`channel`): The heads' diameter in CSS pixels: a number, or a column mapped through size_scale (by default onto the automatic size range). Default: `5` px.

Also these options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill`, `color`, `width`, `opacity`, `outline_color`, `outline_opacity`, `outline_width`.

#### Scales

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `fill_scale`, `color_scale`, `colormap`, `size_scale`, `width_scale`, `outline_color_scale`, `opacity_scale`.

#### Display

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `label`, `legend`, `visible`, `domains`, `blend`, `glow`, `shade`, `options`, `name`.

#### Interaction

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `identity`, `select`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `nearest`, `respond`, `selection_opacity`, `enter_effect`, `exit_effect`.

#### Animation

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `animation`, `animation_duration`, `animation_easing`.

#### Symbol rotation

- `rotation` (`number`): The symbol's rotation. Default: `0` degrees.

#### Symbol

- `shape` (`string | column | string[]`): The point symbol: a shape name, a column of categories mapped to shapes, or one name per row. Default: `"circle"`.
- `shape_scale` (`scale`): A categorical() scale from the shape column's categories to shape names.

#### Size units

- `size_units` (`"px" | "data"`): What size measures: CSS pixels whatever the zoom, or units of the x axis, so zooming scales the points. Default: `"px"`.

#### Legend settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `legend_font_size`, `legend_font_family`, `legend_text_color`, `legend_tick_format`.

#### Color settings

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `quantize`, `levels`.

#### Limits

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `max_elements`.

#### The mark's own axes

These options the marks share (described on Mark options): `x_transform`, `x_invert`, `xbounds`, `xrange`, `y_transform`, `y_invert`, `ybounds`, `yrange`, `z_transform`, `z_invert`, `zbounds`, `zrange`.

#### Geometry

- `detail` (`number`, setting): How finely a point's or a surface's geometry is divided (sphere segments, grid cells).

#### Shading

- `lit` (`boolean`, setting): Shade the mark with the plot's lights. Default: `False`.
- `transparent` (`boolean`, setting): Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks. Default: `False`.

#### Advanced renderer options

- `max_instances` (`number | null`): The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row. Default: `None`.

### Usage

A stem from `baseline` (a number or a column, default 0) to each `y`, on either side of it, with a point at the end. Stems run along y, or along x when `y` is the categorical column (`orientation` overrides the detection); `z` places both parts in 3D. Style the stems with their `stem` object (`stem={{ color: "gray", width: 2, dash: [2, 2] }}` in Svelte, `stem={"color": "gray", "width": 2, "dash": [2, 2]}` in Python), or with `theme.marks.Lollipop.color` and `.width`. `stemColor` and `stemWidth` are removed; use `stem.color` and `stem.width`.
